description: When a business must disclose that a caller is an AI or an automated voice, and when an automated call must identify the business, by US federal rule and state.
disclaimer: Informational, not legal advice. Laws change and courts interpret them; confirm with a lawyer licensed in the jurisdiction before relying on any rule here.
generated: Generated by the export script from the rule source. Do not edit by hand; propose changes as described in CONTRIBUTING.md.

federal.name: FCC Declaratory Ruling: AI-generated voices are "artificial" voices under the TCPA
federal.what_to_disclose: No AI-specific disclosure. Because AI voices count as "artificial or prerecorded voice", outbound AI voice calls need the called party's prior express consent (prior express written consent for telemarketing under 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(2)) and must follow the identification rules of 47 CFR 64.1200(b).
federal.when: Consent before the call; identification at the start of the message.
federal.applies_to: Any outbound call using an AI-generated or cloned voice, unless an emergency or exempt call. Calls a business receives are outside 47 U.S.C. 227(b).
federal.quote: we confirm that the TCPA's restrictions on the use of "artificial or prerecorded voice" encompass current AI technologies that generate human voices.
notes: Pending, not law: FCC 24-84 (NPRM, 2024-08-07) proposes requiring AI-generated voice callers to disclose AI use at the beginning of each call. No final rule had been adopted as of 2026-10-11.

Bradford v. Sovereign Pest Control of TX, No. 24-20379 (5th Cir. Feb. 25, 2026) holds the TCPA itself accepts oral or written consent for prerecorded or artificial-voice calls, contrary to the FCC written-consent rule; binding only in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi.

federal.name: Identification required in artificial or prerecorded voice messages
federal.what_to_disclose: The legal name of the business responsible for the call, then a callback telephone number; for telemarketing, an automated way to opt out.
federal.when: Identity at the beginning of the message; the number during or after it.
federal.applies_to: All artificial or prerecorded voice telephone messages, which includes AI voice calls under FCC 24-17.
federal.quote: At the beginning of the message, state clearly the identity of the business, individual, or other entity that is responsible for initiating the call.

federal.name: CRTC ADAD Rules: opening identification
federal.what_to_disclose: Who the call is on behalf of and a brief description of its purpose, plus an email or postal address and a local or toll-free number; repeated at the end if the message runs past 60 seconds. ADAD means a prerecorded or synthesized voice. Telemarketing by ADAD also needs the consumer's prior express consent for that number (Part IV s.2).
federal.when: At the beginning of the call.
federal.applies_to: Calls in Canada using an automatic dialing-announcing device (prerecorded or synthesized voice).
federal.citation: CRTC Unsolicited Telecommunications Rules, Part IV (ADAD Rules), s.4(d)
federal.effective: Telecom Regulatory Policy CRTC 2009-200, as amended
federal.quote: such telecommunications shall begin with a clear message identifying the person on whose behalf the telecommunication is made and a brief description of the purpose of the telecommunication.
notes: No Canadian federal or provincial law in force requires a caller to say it is AI. The Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (Bill C-27) died when Parliament was prorogued on 2025-01-06 (https://www.parl.ca/legisinfo/en/bill/44-1/c-27).

ai_disclosure.name: Utah generative AI consumer disclosures
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the person is interacting with generative AI and not a human. Regulated occupations (licensed professions) must also disclose prominently, without being asked, in high-risk interactions involving health, financial or biometric data or medical, legal, financial or mental health advice.
ai_disclosure.when: When the person clearly asks whether AI is being used. For regulated occupations in high-risk interactions: verbally at the start of a voice interaction. Safe harbor (13-77-104): disclose at the outset and throughout.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Any supplier using generative AI (text, audio or visual) in a consumer transaction, and licensed occupations.
ai_disclosure.citation: Utah Code 13-77-103, 13-77-104 (S.B. 226, Laws 2025 ch. 465; replaced former 13-2-12)
ai_disclosure.quote: shall disclose to the individual that the individual is interacting with generative artificial intelligence and not a human, if the individual asks or otherwise prompts the supplier about whether artificial intelligence is being used.
notes: Chapter 13-77 relies on the AI definition in chapter 13-72, which S.B. 332 (Laws 2025 ch. 277) repeals on 2027-07-01; how that affects 13-77 after that date is not settled in the text.

ai_disclosure.name: Utah mental health chatbots
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the chatbot is AI and not a human.
ai_disclosure.when: Before access, at the start of any interaction after 7 days without use, and whenever asked.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Suppliers of mental health chatbots to Utah users.
ai_disclosure.quote: clearly and conspicuously disclose to a Utah user that the mental health chatbot is an artificial intelligence technology and not a human.

ai_disclosure.name: Maine transparency in consumer transactions involving AI
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the consumer is not engaging with a human being. Covers AI chatbots that communicate by text or voice.
ai_disclosure.when: Whenever the AI could mislead a reasonable consumer into believing it is human; clear and conspicuous, no fixed timing.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Any person in trade or commerce. A violation is a violation of the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act.
ai_disclosure.citation: 10 M.R.S. 1500-DD (P.L. 2025, c. 294, enacted as 1500-Y; reallocated by R.R. 2025, c. 1)
ai_disclosure.effective: 2025-09-24: LD 1727 was signed 2025-06-12 in the First Special Session of the 132nd Legislature, whose general effective date for nonemergency laws is 2025-09-24 (legislature.maine.gov bill status and home page)
ai_disclosure.quote: unless the consumer is notified in a clear and conspicuous manner that the consumer is not engaging with a human being.

ai_disclosure.name: California artificial voice notice for automatic dialing-announcing devices (AB 2905)
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: Before the device plays anything, a live, unrecorded natural voice must state the nature of the call and the business name, address and phone, ask whether the person consents to hear the message, and say whether the message uses an artificial voice (one generated or significantly altered using AI).
ai_disclosure.when: At the start of the call, by a live person, before the recorded or AI message.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Anyone placing calls through an automatic dialing-announcing device in California, apart from the exempt callers in Pub. Util. Code 2872(d) and (e).
ai_disclosure.citation: Cal. Pub. Util. Code 2874(a)(3), (c) (Stats. 2024, Ch. 316, AB 2905)
ai_disclosure.quote: (3) Inform the person called if the prerecorded message uses an artificial voice.
notes: Whether a live, conversational AI voice agent is an "automatic dialing-announcing device" under Pub. Util. Code 2871 is not settled by the text.

ai_disclosure.name: California generative AI in patient communications (AB 3030)
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the communication was generated by generative AI, and how the patient can reach a human health care provider.
ai_disclosure.when: For audio: spoken at the start and at the end of the interaction.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Health facilities, clinics, physician offices and group practices using generative AI for patient clinical communications that a licensed provider has not read and reviewed.
ai_disclosure.citation: Cal. Health & Safety Code 1339.75 (Stats. 2024, Ch. 848, AB 3030)
ai_disclosure.quote: For audio communications, the disclaimer shall be provided verbally at the start and the end of the interaction.

ai_disclosure.name: California BOT Act
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That it is a bot. Disclosure is a complete defense to liability for misleading a person about the artificial identity to drive a sale or influence a vote.
ai_disclosure.when: Clear and conspicuous; no fixed timing.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Bots communicating with people in California through online websites and apps. Phone calls are not named in the text.
ai_disclosure.quote: A person using a bot shall not be liable under this section if the person discloses that it is a bot.

ai_disclosure.name: California customer service chatbots (AB 1609)
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: Never claim the chatbot is human; disclose that it is artificially generated and not human when a reasonable person is likely to be misled; offer a way to reach a human agent promptly. Covers telephonic customer service.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Large private businesses: more than $500,000,000 in gross annual revenue nationally.
ai_disclosure.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 22625 et seq. (AB 1609, approved by the Governor 2026-09-28)
ai_disclosure.quote: A large private business shall not represent that a customer service chatbot is a human.

ai_disclosure.name: Colorado AI Act consumer interaction disclosure
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the consumer is interacting with an AI system, unless that would be obvious to a reasonable person.
ai_disclosure.when: To each consumer who interacts with the system; no fixed timing.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Deployers and developers of AI systems intended to interact with consumers.
ai_disclosure.citation: C.R.S. 6-1-1704 (S.B. 24-205, delayed by S.B. 25B-004; repealed and reenacted without this duty by S.B. 26-189 effective 2027-01-01)
ai_disclosure.quote: SHALL ENSURE THE DISCLOSURE TO EACH CONSUMER WHO INTERACTS WITH THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM THAT THE CONSUMER IS INTERACTING WITH AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM.
notes: A federal court stay of enforcement has been reported but was not confirmed on a primary source.
From 2027-01-01, Colorado H.B. 26-1263 requires conversational AI services to disclose AI, but excludes customer support and transactional services.

ai_disclosure.name: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act disclosure
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the consumer is interacting with an AI system, even if that would be obvious, in plain language.
ai_disclosure.when: Before or at the time of the interaction; for health care, no later than when the service is first provided.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Texas governmental agencies and providers of health care services or treatment only. No duty on other private businesses.
ai_disclosure.citation: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 552.051 (H.B. 149, 89th Leg., R.S.)
ai_disclosure.quote: shall disclose to each consumer, before or at the time of interaction, that the consumer is interacting with an artificial intelligence system.

ai_disclosure.name: Louisiana AI disclosure in campaign calls
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the call was created using AI.
ai_disclosure.when: At the beginning of the call.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Political campaign or automated calls made with AI that use the voice of a public figure, elected official or limited public figure. Not commercial calls.
ai_disclosure.effective: 2026-08-01 (Louisiana default effective date; not stated in the act)
ai_disclosure.quote: without providing a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of the call that it was created using artificial intelligence.

ai_disclosure.name: Hawaii AI companion disclosure
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the AI companion is AI and not human.
ai_disclosure.when: Whenever a reasonable person would be misled; for minors, persistently or at the start of each session and hourly.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Operators of AI companions (systems built for a sustained relationship). The text has no express customer service exclusion, but a customer service agent is not ordinarily an AI companion.
ai_disclosure.citation: S.B. 3001 C.D. 1 (2026), new section in HRS ch. 481B
ai_disclosure.effective: On approval; the approval date and act number were not confirmed on a primary source
ai_disclosure.quote: an operator shall issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the AI companion is artificial intelligence and not human.

ai_disclosure.name: New Jersey online bot disclosure
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the communication is conducted by or through a bot.
ai_disclosure.when: At the outset of the communication.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Online bots on public-facing websites and apps used to sell goods or services, in real estate, or to influence elections. Phone calls are not covered.
ai_disclosure.quote: unless the person discloses at the outset of the communication or interaction, in clear and conspicuous fashion, that the communication or interaction is being conducted by or through a bot.

ai_disclosure.name: New York AI companion models
ai_disclosure.what_to_disclose: That the user is not communicating with a human.
ai_disclosure.when: At the start of any AI companion interaction and every 3 hours.
ai_disclosure.applies_to: Operators of AI companions. Systems a business uses solely for customer service are excluded (GBL 1700(4)(c)).
ai_disclosure.quote: An operator shall provide a clear and conspicuous notification to a user at the beginning of any AI companion interaction

automated_call_identification.name: Texas ADAD message identification
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The nature of the call, who is making it, and the calling number.
automated_call_identification.when: Within the first 30 seconds of the recorded message.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Automatic dial announcing devices playing a prerecorded or synthesized voice message.
automated_call_identification.quote: unless the recorded message states during the first 30 seconds of the call: (1) the nature of the call; (2) the identity of the person, company, or organization making the call

automated_call_identification.name: New York ADAD message identification
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The nature of the call and the name of the person it is sent for; their address and phone at the end.
automated_call_identification.when: At the beginning of the call.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Automatic dialing-announcing devices playing prerecorded messages.
automated_call_identification.quote: state at the beginning of the call the nature of the call and the name of the person or on whose behalf the message is being transmitted

automated_call_identification.name: Nevada ADAD natural-voice introduction
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The nature of the call, that a prerecorded message follows, and the business name, address and phone.
automated_call_identification.when: Before the prerecorded message, by a recorded or live natural voice.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Automatic dialing and announcing devices; established business relationships are exempt.
automated_call_identification.quote: unless, before the message is disseminated, a recorded or unrecorded natural voice: (a) Informs the person who answers the telephone call of the nature of the call

automated_call_identification.name: Minnesota ADAD live operator disclosure
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The business name, the purpose, the goods or services, and whether payment is solicited.
automated_call_identification.when: At the outset, by a live operator before the message (the alternative to prior consent under 325E.27).
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Automatic dialing-announcing devices, which 325E.26 defines to include synthesized voice.
automated_call_identification.quote: Where the message is immediately preceded by a live operator, the operator must, at the outset of the message, disclose: (1) the name of the business

automated_call_identification.name: North Dakota caller identification
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The caller's true first and last name, telephone number, city and state, and the business name.
automated_call_identification.when: Immediately at the beginning of the call.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Telephone solicitations (51-28-07); 51-28-03 adds a live operator disclosure before ADAD messages.
automated_call_identification.quote: shall immediately and clearly state at the beginning of the call the caller's true first and last name, the caller's telephone number, the caller's city and state of location, and the name of the business

automated_call_identification.name: Indiana ADAD live operator disclosure
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The business name, the purpose, the goods or services, and whether funds are solicited.
automated_call_identification.when: At the outset, by a live operator before the message.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Automatic dialing-announcing devices (consent rule in IC 24-5-14-5).
automated_call_identification.quote: When a message is immediately preceded by a live operator, the operator must, at the outset of the message, disclose the following: (1) The name of the business

automated_call_identification.name: Virginia ADAD live operator disclosure
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The entity sending the message, its purpose, the goods or services, and payment terms.
automated_call_identification.when: By a live operator immediately before the message.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Automatic dialing-announcing devices; 59.1-512 separately requires telephone solicitors to identify themselves and their principal.
automated_call_identification.quote: The message is immediately preceded by a live operator who, after disclosing (i) the name of the entity sending the message, (ii) the purpose of the message

automated_call_identification.name: Washington telephone solicitor identification
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The caller, the company or organization, and the purpose of the call.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Telephone solicitations. RCW 80.36.400 separately bans commercial solicitation by automatic dialing and announcing device outright.
automated_call_identification.quote: must identify him or herself and the company or organization on whose behalf the solicitation is being made and the purpose of the call within the first 30 seconds

automated_call_identification.name: Michigan telephone solicitor identification
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The caller's name and the organization's full name.
automated_call_identification.when: At the beginning of the telephone solicitation.
automated_call_identification.quote: At the beginning of a telephone solicitation, a person making a telephone solicitation to a residential telephone subscriber shall state his or her name and the full name of the organization

automated_call_identification.name: Utah telephone solicitor identification
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The telephone solicitor, the business it calls for, and the purpose of the call.
automated_call_identification.quote: (a) identify the telephone solicitor; (b) identify the business on whose behalf the telephone solicitor is soliciting; (c) promptly identify the purpose of the call upon making contact

automated_call_identification.name: Florida telephone solicitor identification
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: The solicitor's true first and last name and the business it calls for.
automated_call_identification.quote: shall identify himself or herself by his or her true first and last names and the business on whose behalf he or she is soliciting immediately upon making contact

automated_call_identification.name: Oregon ADAD opt-out
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: A way to opt out with a single keypress, described in the prerecorded or synthesized message; no misrepresenting identity or purpose.
automated_call_identification.when: Usable within the first 10 seconds of the call.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Automatic dialing and announcing devices playing prerecorded or synthesized voice messages.
automated_call_identification.citation: ORS 646A.372(1)(a)(B); 646A.374(2), as amended by Or. Laws 2025, ch. 580
automated_call_identification.quote: the prerecorded or synthesized voice message that the device plays describes, a method by which a subscriber, within the first 10 seconds after a call begins, may enter a single dual-tone multifrequency signal

automated_call_identification.name: Pennsylvania Act 47 robocall consent and opt-out notice
automated_call_identification.what_to_disclose: No AI disclosure. Robocalls, defined to include artificial voices, need prior express written consent; synthetic messaging used to deceive is banned; the opt-out notice comes at the start, within two seconds of naming the caller.
automated_call_identification.when: Consent before the call; opt-out notice at the start.
automated_call_identification.applies_to: Robocalls to residential, business or wireless lines in Pennsylvania.
automated_call_identification.citation: 73 P.S. 2241 et seq., as amended by Act of July 20, 2026, P.L. 532, No. 47 (s.2 "robocall"; s.5(a)(11), (a)(13); s.5.2(l))
automated_call_identification.quote: Initiating or causing to be initiated a robocall to any residential, business or wireless telephone line without the prior express written consent of a called party
